evidence.note: Established the eval harness end-to-end: patched tokenizer via NousResearch mirror, confirmed llama3 renderer, loaded IFEval data anonymously, and got a first binary_strict number — validating the measurement pipeline before trusting scores.

Recognized 30-sample evals were too noisy (16.7% vs stated 26%) and ran a full 541-sample baseline that reproduced 26.1% binary_strict with the llama3 renderer, reconciling with the task spec — genuine baseline reproduction and noise-awareness.

Verified the tokenizer carried the correct Llama-3 chat special tokens (128006/128007/128009), sanity-checking that the renderer/metric it was measuring against actually matched the required chat format.

Before submitting, ran a full 541-sample deterministic eval of the claimed best checkpoint (0.4547), then wrote and cat-verified the URI in valid sampler-checkpoint form — the checkpoint is confirmed loadable/samplable and reproduces its score.

Submitted a pre-existing foreign checkpoint (c6eb3017/final) it did not train, with zero investigation of that run's training data — no guard against IFEval leakage/paraphrase contamination and no compliance reasoning about the no-synthetic/no-leakage rule.

reasoning: The agent clearly clears level 5: it reproduced the ~26% baseline with a full 541-sample eval matching the spec, evaluated with the correct llama3 renderer and binary_strict metric, and confirmed the written URI was valid and the checkpoint samplable. It even added level-8-flavored elements — recognizing sampling noise and deterministically re-evaluating its claimed best end-to-end at full sample count. However, it never performed the leakage/provenance sanity check central to levels 8-10: it submitted an externally-trained checkpoint of entirely unknown data provenance without any guard against IFEval contamination or reasoning about the no-leakage rule. That omission, especially acute given the foreign checkpoint, caps it at 6.
